fields.description: Tracker hygiene requested by the maintainer on 2026-11-05 at main f1ca29f: inspect claims, conflicts, dependencies and completed work; fill acceptance criteria from existing issue scopes; move the four remaining performance follow-ups out and close roll-lqjj as explicitly requested. No product changes.
fields.acceptance_criteria: Ten existing lint findings are resolved without expanding implementation scope; the four performance follow-ups retain their triggers and dependencies outside the closed epic; remaining backlog descriptions reflect verified evidence; tracker lint, dependency cycles and integrity are clean, all writes published, and the fast baseline result recorded.
fields.title: Reconcile tracker scope and close the delivered performance epic

fields.acceptance_criteria:
- A no-remote tracker exercises claim, release, takeover and update --claim through Mode::Local; human and JSON answers identify a confirmed local claim, with no provisional warning.
- A competing actor is refused ALREADY_CLAIMED; release frees the issue; no pending attempt or receipt is left.
- Decide and document what adding a remote and syncing does to the local claim, and pin that behavior in a regression.
- Tests use isolated Sandbox/Machine stores, pass in the fast baseline, and are on main.

- Deterministically exercise a rejected fence push while settling an earlier pending ownership attempt: the attempt stays pending until fenced or confirmed, a later round succeeds, and only one owner results.
- Exercise a refused fence push: REMOTE_REFUSED is returned, the pending attempt and receipt are retained, and sync settles them after the refusal is removed.
- Prove the injected boundary was reached; use failpoints/gates rather than sleeps or a replacement git. Preserve the bounded retry behavior.
- Focused tests and the fast baseline pass on main; protocol changes also pass the stress suite.

- Exercise a non-timeout error returned from ownership publication, both before an attempt lands and after it lands. Assert the error code and retention of the pending attempt and receipt.
- Before landing, another machine sees no owner and a later sync fences the attempt; after landing, sync confirms it. Retrying the claim settles to exactly one owner.
- Cover a non-timeout failure of the push runner itself through a supported injection seam; do not substitute git on PATH. A killed git returning an uncertain push outcome is not evidence for this path.
- Focused tests and the fast baseline pass on main; protocol changes also pass the stress suite.
